# 1 Samuel Chapter 8 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 154r--154v | **Source Image:** 1SA_008_page_001.jpg, 1SA_008_page_002.jpg

---

**8:1** And-it-was when was-old Samuel, and-he-appointed his-sons [as] judges for-Israel.

**8:2** And-was [the]-name of-his-son, the-firstborn, Joel, and-[the]-name of-his-second, Abijah -- judges in-Beer-sheba.

**8:3** And-not walked his-sons in-his-ways, and-they-turned-aside after the-unjust-gain, and-they-took bribes, and-they-perverted justice.

**8:4** And-gathered-themselves all [the]-elders of-Israel, and-they-came unto Samuel to-the-Ramah.

**8:5** And-they-said unto-him, \"Behold, you are-old, and-your-sons have-not walked in-your-ways. Now appoint for-us a-king to-judge-us like-all the-nations.\"

**8:6** And-was-evil the-thing in-[the]-eyes of-Samuel when they-said, \"Give to-us a-king to-judge-us.\" And-prayed Samuel unto YHWH.

**8:7** And-said YHWH unto Samuel, \"Listen to-[the]-voice of-the-people in-all which they-say unto-you, for not you have-they-rejected, but me they-have-rejected from-reigning over-them.

**8:8** According-to-all the-deeds which they-have-done from-the-day I-brought-them-up from-Egypt and-unto this-day -- and-they-forsook-me and-they-served gods other -- so they [are]-doing also to-you.

**8:9** And-now listen to-their-voice; however, you-shall-surely-warn them, and-you-shall-declare to-them [the]-manner of-the-king who will-reign over-them.\"

**8:10** And-said Samuel all [the]-words of-YHWH unto the-people, the-ones-asking from-him a-king.

**8:11** And-he-said, \"This will-be [the]-manner of-the-king who will-reign over-you: your-sons he-will-take and-he-will-set [them] for-himself in-his-chariot and-in-his-horsemen, and-they-will-run before his-chariot.

**8:12** And-to-set for-himself commanders of-thousands and-commanders of-fifties, and-to-plow his-plowing and-to-reap his-harvest, and-to-make his-instruments of-war and-instruments of-his-chariots.

**8:13** And-your-daughters he-will-take for-perfumers and-for-cooks and-for-bakers.

**8:14** And-your-fields and-your-vineyards and-your-olive-groves, the-best, he-will-take and-he-will-give to-his-servants.

**8:15** And-your-seed and-your-vineyards he-will-tithe, and-he-will-give to-his-officers and-to-his-servants.

**8:16** And-your-male-servants and-your-female-servants and-your-young-men, the-best, and-your-donkeys he-will-take, and-he-will-use [them] for-his-work.

**8:17** Your-flocks he-will-tithe, and-you -- you-will-be to-him as-servants.

**8:18** And-you-will-cry-out on-that-day from-before your-king whom you-have-chosen for-yourselves, and-not will-answer YHWH you on-that-day.\"

**8:19** And-refused the-people to-listen to-[the]-voice of-Samuel, and-they-said, \"No! But a-king shall-be over-us.

**8:20** And-we-will-be, also we, like-all the-nations, and-shall-judge-us our-king, and-he-will-go-out before-us and-he-will-fight our-battles.\"

**8:21** And-heard Samuel all [the]-words of-the-people, and-he-spoke-them in-[the]-ears of-YHWH.

**8:22** And-said YHWH unto Samuel, \"Listen to-their-voice and-you-shall-make-reign for-them a-king.\" And-said Samuel unto [the]-men of-Israel, \"Go, each-man to-his-city.\"

---
## EMET\\\'s Textual Notes

1. **8:7 -- \"not you have they rejected, but me they have rejected\":** The Hebrew כִּי לֹא אֹתְךָ מָאָסוּ כִּי אֹתִי מָאָסוּ -- the double כִּי construction is emphatic. YHWH interprets the request for a king as a direct rejection of divine kingship. This is the theological center of the chapter.

2. **8:9 -- *mishpat ha-melekh* (manner of the king):** The term מִשְׁפַּט here does not mean \"justice\" (its usual sense) but \"customary right/manner\" -- what the king will claim as his prerogative. This is a prophetic warning, not a legal charter.

3. **8:11-17 -- The king\\\'s *mishpat*:** The catalogue of royal prerogatives parallels ancient Near Eastern royal practices, particularly those known from Ugaritic administrative texts. The repeated verb יִקָּח (\"he will take\") structures the entire warning.

4. **8:16 -- \"your young men, the best\" (*bahurekhem ha-tovim*):** The Leningrad Codex reads בַּחוּרֵיכֶם (your young men). The LXX reads \"your cattle\" (τὰ βουκόλια ὑμῶν, reading בְּקַרְכֶם). EMET follows the MT.

5. **8:18 -- \"and YHWH will not answer you\":** The verb יַעֲנֶה is emphatic by position. The irony is stark: the people cry out to YHWH because of the very king they demanded in place of YHWH.

-- EMET
